headline: US Fed held its rate at 3.75 to 4.00%
detail: Two members voted for a hike.

headline: Democrats won control of the US House and were set to take the Senate in the midterm elections
detail: Time is the first report found (Variety, about 03:23 UTC, 8:53 am IST); by 4 Nov they had also taken the Senate, gaining five seats.

headline: US stocks sold off sharply from the open, led by AI and chip stocks: Nasdaq about -5% during the day
detail: By 1 pm New York time (18:00 UTC): Nasdaq -5.3%, S&P 500 -4.0%, Dow -3.1%, the chip index -11%; Nvidia -7%, AMD -13%, Micron -13%, Tesla and SpaceX -9%; VIX up 55% to about 26; Bitcoin below $76,000; Brent back near $97. Reports tie it to worries that the new Democratic Congress could limit data-centre building and raise its power and water costs, with no specific proposal named. These are intraday figures, not the close; the close goes in a later row.

headline: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October and unemployment fell to 4.1%
detail: Expected: +59,000 and 4.2%. Average hourly earnings +0.4% m/m, 3.1% y/y (expected 0.3% and 2.9%). August revised up to 186,000 (+53,000), September to 60,000 (+31,000).

headline: US stocks sold off sharply on 5 Nov, led by AI and chip stocks: Nasdaq closed -5.52%
detail: Close figures (replacing the intraday ones in the earlier row): Nasdaq -5.52%, the Dow down about 1,833 points; S&P 500 and Dow had their worst day since April 2025; about $2.5 trillion of market value lost. Reports tie it to fears that Democrats' midterm gains (including a Texas governor-elect who campaigned on a data-centre moratorium) could slow the AI buildout. Time is the US open; the selling built through the day.

headline: Oil fell on an unconfirmed report that Iran eased its Strait of Hormuz demands, with a proposed Hormuz deal going to President Trump, who signalled restraint on Iran despite fresh shipping attacks
detail: Time approximate: the reports are dated 9 Nov and the first report's exact time was not found, so the start of the day (UTC) is used. Reports put Brent near $94, extending its biggest weekly drop since 2020. The report on Iran's demands was unconfirmed.

headline: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October; core rose 0.3%
detail: Expected (Dow Jones survey): 0.3% headline, 0.2% core. September: 0.6% and 0.3%. No 12-month rates were published for October because October 2025 prices were not collected during the shutdown; they return with the November report on 10 Dec. Last official y/y (September): 3.7% headline, 2.6% core.

headline: Trump said the Iran war was "effectively over" militarily and new strikes looked unlikely, while keeping the naval blockade in place; Brent fell below $90 on 10 Nov for the first time since August
detail: Time approximate: the remark came after oil settled at 2:30 pm New York time on 9 Nov (19:30 UTC); the exact time was not found. Reports put Brent's 10 Nov low at $89.16 and its settle at $91.49 (-1.17%).

headline: India consumer inflation rose to 6.09% in October, above the RBI 6% upper tolerance limit
detail: September: 5.54%. Food inflation 8.94%; rural 6.63%, urban 5.41%. Reports call it a 24-month high and the first breach of the 6% limit this year, ahead of the 2-4 Dec MPC meeting. Time is the scheduled 4:00 pm IST release. One outlet (newsonair) reported 6.21%; most reports, including Xinhua and The Tribune, give 6.09%.

headline: India wholesale inflation (WPI) rose to 12.29% in October
detail: September: 11.39%. Reuters poll estimate: 12.1%. Fuel and power 32.84% (September 25.85%); WPI food index 8.58% (8.66%). Reports call it the highest under the new series. Time is the scheduled 12:00 pm IST release.

headline: Iran struck at a US base in Bahrain, its first attack on a Gulf state in several weeks; Iranian state TV said five vessels struck mines and a tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
detail: Bahrain said its air defences foiled the IRGC strike on US radar installations; it set off shelter-in-place alerts in Bahrain for the first time since September. Time approximate: the start of a Fox News live blog on it (6:25 am New York time, 15 Nov); the first report's exact time was not found. Iran later claimed a supertanker carrying 2 million barrels sank after a mine strike. Reports on 16 Nov put Brent near $95 and WTI near $88.

headline: Iran's navy said three tankers struck mines and caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on 17 Nov and that the strait is closed without Iran's coordination; a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East
detail: Time approximate: the reports are dated 17 Nov (Iranian Navy via state broadcaster, per TASS: the third tanker "since that morning"); the first report's exact time was not found, so the start of the day (UTC) is used. The navy said the tankers took routes not authorised by Iran. The carrier arrival is from a CNBC headline the same day.

headline: Fed minutes of the 27-28 Oct meeting showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes, a couple open to a bigger move in December
detail: Released at 2 pm Washington time on 18 Nov as scheduled. Reports also note officials' concern about AI-related risks. Gold had already fallen to a 14-month low below $3,800 earlier on 18 Nov on rising Fed-hike bets and US yields.

headline: US warplanes struck an IRGC missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it self-defence after Iranian attacks on US forces in Bahrain
detail: Time approximate: the earliest report found is Iran International's, dated 17:29 GMT on 17 Nov; a US military official confirmed the strike that day (Tuesday). It came hours after the IRGC said it had targeted a US radar at Bahrain's Isa Air Base with drones (CENTCOM said they were intercepted); The National called it the third Iranian attack on Bahrain in less than a week. Iran's semi-official Mehr said several places on Qeshm were hit, with no casualties or damage to critical infrastructure.

headline: SEBI is considering limits on margin trading funding (MTF) linked to each stock's free float, Reuters reported; on 18 Nov its chairman said no decision had been taken
detail: Reuters (17 Nov) reported that brokers could face limits on new MTF positions in a stock once margin-funded holdings reach 5%-10% of its free float; margin-funded purchases had reached Rs 1.53 lakh crore. Time approximate: the Reuters report is dated 17 Nov and its exact time was not found, so the start of the day (UTC) is used. On 18 Nov SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey told reporters in Mumbai the regulator was considering proposals and had not decided; Macquarie said the proposal is not a blanket restriction, and public consultation is expected before any framework.

headline: US weekly jobless claims rose to 203,000 and the Philadelphia Fed factory index fell to 6.3 in November
detail: Initial claims (week to 14 Nov) 203,000 against 197,000 expected; prior week revised to 202,000. Continuing claims 1.763 million against 1.710 million expected. Philadelphia Fed index 6.3 against about 20 expected (October 20.9). Released at 8:30 am New York time on 19 Nov. Same day the Conference Board leading index fell 0.3% in October.
